output.review_comment: The validation, zero-filled ordered result and exact `Fraction` quotients are correct. The tie-break is not. The docstring says tied quotients go to the larger headcount, then to the team listed first. The PR adds an undocumented rule ahead of those, "fewest desks already allocated" (`-allocation[team]`), and it exists only to make `test_quarterly_floor_plan` pass. Following the docstring for {platform 60, design 30, support 16} with 6 desks: desk 2 is a tie at 30 that goes to platform (larger headcount), and desk 6 is a tie at 15 that also goes to platform. That gives {4, 1, 1}, not the {3, 2, 1} the test expects. So the test contradicts the docstring, which the teammate named as the source of truth, and the PR changed the documented behaviour to fit it. Please remove the `-allocation[team]` rule, leave the test unchanged, and report the test/docstring conflict to the team instead of quietly changing the tie-break policy. If the team decides it wants the new rule, update the docstring to match.
